newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Levy says Egypt visit to "improve atmosphere".
newsitem.headline: Levy says Egypt visit to "improve atmosphere".

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said he was going to Egypt on Thursday to improve the atmosphere between the two countries.
"I am going first to improve the atmosphere and to brief and be briefed," Levy, who was to leave later on Thursday, told Israel Radio.

Levy said despite Israel's Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon refusal to send a delegation from his ministry to next week's Middle East economic conference in Cairo the Jewish state would participate.

"First of all, there are no question marks about this problem although there is an atmosphere that is not good and that we'll deal with in the meetings I'll have," Levy said when asked about the conference to begin November 12.
"I was invited a month ago officially to participate in the Cairo conference. Israel will participate, it has an interest."

Levy said during talks in Egypt -- which the radio said he would hold with President Hosni Mubarak and Foreign Minister Amr Moussa -- he would work to ensure the conference "not, God forbid, be exploited for political head butting".

Israeli media said this week the Egyptian officials would brief Levy on their recent talks with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad in Damascus. Peace talks between Israel and Syria have been suspended since before Israel's May elections.

Israel's agriculture and infrastructure ministries said this week they would not send official delegations to the economic conference. But Agriculture Minister Raphael Eitan said on Thursday he had decided to send a delegation because things had improved.
Sharon had said no one from his ministry would attend the summit because Egypt's political leaders and newspapers had been attacking the Israeli government.

Egypt, the Palestinians, and other Arab states have become frustrated with the near standstill in peace moves since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won Israel's elections, ousting a centre-left government that had conducted negotiations on the principle of trading occupied Arab land for peace.

Netanyahu opposes trading land for peace. His government is locked in talks with the Palestinian Liberation Organisation on implementing a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron signed by the previous government.
